note: After the genus-level monograph of Roonwal & Chhotani (1989) (in English), whose account is adapted from the original description of Roonwal & Verma 1973; all three castes are described and measured (the alate only from dealated individuals). Type locality Didwana, Nagaur District, Rajasthan, India.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head pale brown, the thorax and abdomen paler; antennae dirty brownish white; postclypeus tinged with brown; compound eyes black; labrum whitish; mandibles dark brown, the margins nearly black; legs dirty white, the tibiae pale brown. Head and body with moderate pilosity, of long and short hairs. Body length of dealated individuals about 8.9 mm. Head capsule nearly round (length to the mandibular base 1.47, width including the compound eyes 1.47 mm); frons weakly inclined in front. Anteclypeus slightly raised, trapezoidal, translucent; postclypeus wider than long. Compound eyes large, nearly oval, maximum diameter 0.45 mm. Ocelli oval, white spots, touching the compound eyes. Antennae 11—12-segmented; segment 4 shortest. Labrum large, translucent, dome-shaped, with a few small hairs all over. Mandibles as in the genus. Pronotum large, nearly trapezoidal, the sides nearly rounded; wider than the head including the compound eyes (width 1.74, maximum length 0.95 mm); anterior margin concave, posterior margin slightly convex, neither margin with a median notch. Mesonotum and metanotum narrower than the pronotum; posterior margin concave, without a median notch. Hind femora short and inflated; hind tibiae slender and long; tibial spur formula 3:3:3; tarsi 4-segmented; arolium absent. Abdomen sparsely hairy; cerci short, 0.18 mm long, 2-segmented; styli short, single-segmented.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Anterior part of the head capsule dark brown, the posterior part paler; base of the mandibles dark brown, the anterior part nearly black; antennae brownish towards the base, paler at the apex; pronotum pale straw-coloured, mesonotum and metanotum paler; abdomen and legs whitish. Head and body with moderate pilosity, with small hairs all over. Body length (including the mandibles) 9.7—10.3 mm. Head capsule nearly rectangular (length to the mandibular base 2.10—2.37, width 1.84—2.00 mm); anterior part weakly constricted; posterior margin weakly concave; frons gently sloping in front; Y-shaped suture invisible. Compound eyes a small, nearly oval black spot, flush with the surface of the head, maximum diameter 0.26 mm. Ocelli absent. Antennae 12—15-segmented (mostly 13-segmented), segment 2 shortest. Anteclypeus narrow, translucent; postclypeus also narrow, dark brown. Labrum translucent, whitish, sparsely hairy, with a weak median point. Mandibles thick and stout, weakly incurved at the apex, the outer margin with an elevation at the base; mandible length 1.63 mm. Left mandible with 5 marginal teeth; right mandible with 2 marginal teeth, situated beyond the midpoint. Postmentum long (median length 1.74 mm), rod-shaped or inverted vase-shaped; widest in front, narrowed into a narrow waist at the posterior quarter (maximum width 0.74—0.79, minimum width 0.37 mm); anterior margin straight; posterior margin wavy (concave in the middle and projecting outwards). Pronotum nearly rectangular, slightly wider than the head (maximum width 2.05—2.21 mm); anterior margin deeply concave, posterior margin weakly convex, neither with a median notch. Mesonotum and metanotum narrower than the pronotum. Legs short, the hind femora extremely inflated, the fore and mid femora less inflated; tibiae short, tibial spur formula 3:3:3; tarsi 4-segmented. Abdomen sparsely hairy; cerci 2-segmented, 0.18 mm long; styli single-segmented, 0.09 mm long.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Pseudoworker: head and mandibles dirty white; mandibular margins nearly black; the rest of the body translucent dirty white. Pilosity moderate. Body length 6.6—8.9 mm. Head capsule nearly round; length to the mandibular base 1.32—1.58, width 1.37—1.58 mm. Compound eyes small, a nearly oval black spot, flush with the surface of the head.
